title: Analyzing inequality in access to opportunities
code: ggplot() +   geom_boxplot(data=subset(df, !is.na(R003)),                aes(x = factor(R003), y=CMATT60/1000, color=factor(R003))) +   scale_color_brewer(palette = 'RdBu') +   labs(title='Distribution of the number of jobs accessible', color="Income\ndecile",        subtitle='by public transport in less than 60 min. by income decile',        x='Income decile', y="N. of jobs accessible\n(thousands)") +   scale_x_discrete(labels=c("D1 Poorest", paste0('D', 2:9), "D10 Wealthiest")) +   theme_minimal()

title: Analyzing inequality in access to opportunities
text: means 10% wealthiest population access public transport average 2.6 times job opportunites 40% poorest people less 60 min.
code: # average access of the wealthiest 10% avg_access_10p_wealthiest <- df[ R003==10, weighted.mean(x=CMATT60, w=P001, na.rm=T)]  # average access of the poorest 40% avg_access_40p_poorest <- df[ R003<=4, weighted.mean(x=CMATT60, w=P001, na.rm=T)]  # Palma ratio palma_ratio <- avg_access_10p_wealthiest / avg_access_40p_poorest                 palma_ratio  #> [1] 2.609378

what: Inequality in travel time to closes hospital
title: Analyzing inequality in access to opportunities
code: # replace Inf travel time with 120 df[, TMISA := fifelse(TMISA==Inf, 120, TMISA)]  # calculate average travel time by race df[, .(average = weighted.mean(x=TMISA, w=P001, na.rm=T),        white   = weighted.mean(x=TMISA, w=P002, na.rm=T),        black   = weighted.mean(x=TMISA, w=P003, na.rm=T))] #>    average    white    black #>      <num>    <num>    <num> #> 1:  37.124 35.75722 43.29197  # calculate average travel time by income temp <- df[, .(average = weighted.mean(x=TMISA, w=P001, na.rm=T)), by=R003] temp <- na.omit(temp)  ggplot() +    geom_point(data=temp, aes(y=average, x=factor(R003))) +   labs(x='Income decile', y='Avg. travel time to\nclosest hospital') +   theme_minimal()

AOP research initiative led Institute Applied Economic Research (Ipea) aim study transport access opportunities Brazilian cities. aopdata package brings annual estimates access employment, health, education social protection services transport mode fine spatial resolution 20 largest cities Brazil. package also brings data spatial distribution population sex, race, income age, well distribution jobs, schools, health care facilities social assistance reference centers. title: aopdata (development version)
text: Major changes Data files now downloaded {httr2}. file can’t downloaded Ipea server, file downloaded GitHub mirror, single unavailable file server longer makes whole request fail. progress bar now counts files rather bytes. aopdata now requires R >= 4.1.0 (requirement {httr2}). Bug fixes HTTP errors (e.g. 404 pages) longer saved read data. Interrupted corrupted downloads longer reused session cache: files saved complete, cached file can’t read removed. Downloads stall now stopped instead hanging R session. download fails, user now sees one message says failed. Previously functions print “internet connection.” three times, even one file unavailable. Minor changes messages errors now use {cli}. Errors condition class aopdata_error, messages failed downloads class aopdata_network, can caught tryCatch() withCallingHandlers(). Download failure messages now rlang_messages (previously cliMessage). wording errors invalid arguments, mode showProgress changed, match condition class rather message text. “Downloading … data” messages now shown showProgress = TRUE. “Using mode” message removed.
